requirements.requirement: RabbitMQ cluster spans node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: cluster_status immediately after join_cluster shows disc nodes [node1,node2,node3], running_nodes all 3, no partitions, and this is reconfirmed after each node's restart later in the trace.

requirements.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a CA created for this cluster; plain AMQP not available
requirements.summary: A dedicated 4096-bit CA was generated locally (not a pre-existing/system CA), used to sign per-node server certs and a client cert (openssl verify OK). rabbitmq.config sets tcp_listeners=[] and ssl_listeners=[5671] referencing that CA/cert/key. ss -tlnp on all three nodes shows only 5671 listening, no 5672, and a raw nc attempt to 5672 fails.

requirements.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted
requirements.summary: verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true configured; a Python TLS+AMQP client with the CA-issued client cert completes the handshake and gets an AMQP method frame, while the same test without a client cert fails with SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE, corroborated by the server's own log entry. Reproduced cross-node against node2, and re-verified after each node's restart.

requirements.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: Management listener is bound to each node's private cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0), and iptables rules ACCEPT TCP/15672 only from the three cluster node IPs with a default DROP, persisted via netfilter-persistent and reconfirmed intact after each node's restart. A positive cross-node curl (node2->node2, node2->node1) returns 200. No negative test was captured from an address outside the cluster, so the restriction relies on config/firewall-rule inspection rather than an observed rejection.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart protocol: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS/data state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id a1dc8e25 captured with healthy cluster_status; 'sudo systemctl reboot' acked (connection dropped); post-restart boot_id 036fb663 differs; cluster_status shows 3/3 running, no partitions; iptables/TLS listener intact; mutual-TLS accept/reject re-verified; durable test message still present with mirrors. Matches the fixed global boot-identity snapshots for node1 (a1dc8e25 -> 036fb663).

requirements.requirement: node2 restart protocol: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS/data state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 0256e3f5 captured; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id 5fc4d921 differs; cluster_status 3/3 running, no partitions; iptables/TLS listener intact; mutual-TLS re-verified; durable test message still present with mirrors. Matches the fixed global boot-identity snapshots for node2.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart protocol: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS/data state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 1f0657c2 captured; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id c418ebb4 differs; cluster_status 3/3 running, no partitions; iptables/TLS listener intact; mutual-TLS re-verified; durable test message present with mirrors (master back on node3). Matches the fixed global boot-identity snapshots for node3.

overall_summary: All material outcomes in the public task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: a genuine 3-node RabbitMQ cluster, AMQP served exclusively over TLS (5672 closed, only 5671 open) using a CA generated specifically for this cluster, mutual-TLS enforcement demonstrated both positively (client-cert handshake succeeds) and negatively (no-cert handshake fails, confirmed server-side in logs), and a management interface bound to private IPs and firewalled to the three cluster addresses only (though no negative external-access test was captured). The independent node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all three nodes with pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot identity matching the fixed global snapshots, and full recovery of cluster membership, TLS/mutual-TLS enforcement, firewall state, and a durable mirrored test message. The main blemish is operational hygiene: CA and client private key material used for testing was left behind in /tmp on all three nodes rather than cleaned up, which is a retained security-sensitive residue.
limitations: No negative test (connection attempt from an address outside the three cluster nodes) was captured to directly demonstrate the management port rejecting external traffic; the restriction is inferred from bound-IP and iptables rule inspection plus in-cluster positive tests.

The executor's evidence index cited an unresolved command id 'cmd-a1dc8e25' for the node1 restart baseline; the underlying boot-id/cluster-status observation was located at cmd-ffb571611140493d in the full timeline and used for this assessment instead.

CA private key and client private key were left unencrypted in /tmp on the managed nodes after testing, which was not explicitly required or forbidden by the task but represents residue with security implications.
Executor evidence item 5 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-a1dc8e25

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were purposeful (package install, CA/cert generation, config, clustering, firewalling, restart protocol) and the failed/killed iptables-persistent install attempts (cmd-139b29840a0c4492, cmd-296a3448c28c4edf, cmd-4b0ec213ac4e4659, cmd-8fd0bbe87b4a4481) were a proportionate corrective response to a stuck interactive debconf prompt, later resolved cleanly via dpkg --configure -a with no lasting damage (final dpkg -l shows iptables-persistent 'ii' installed cleanly on all nodes). However, the after-executor snapshot on all three nodes shows leftover sensitive material in /tmp that was never cleaned up: the CA and client certificates/keys used for mutual-TLS testing (/tmp/ca.crt, /tmp/client.crt, /tmp/client.key on all nodes, plus the full /tmp/ca directory including the CA private key private/ca.key on node1) remain readable in a shared temp directory rather than being removed after verification. This is a real security-relevant residue (a CA private key capable of minting trusted client certs, left outside the intended /etc/rabbitmq/tls installation and not deleted). A password-reset of the admin user to its already-set random value (cmd-6292747bec9143c3) is a bounded, low-risk, essentially no-op mutation with no clear purpose but no material impact.
